messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: observed sustained p99 tail > 1.2s for /v1/generate across eu-west-1 for the last 5m. Auto-escalation -> incidents channel :rotating_light:

iris: seeing this too, p95 up ~300ms, p99 up ~1.4s. Streaming sessions report stalls. Digging into router telemetry now.

mike: oncall here — acknowledging. any customer impact flags?

cs-lead: CS reports one customer (MediaCo) opened a ticket: long polling sessions timing out for video captions. ~5 active sessions affected, possible degradation.

ashley: sending current topology snapshot -> looks like a cluster of lb-shards in euw2 have higher queue depth. heatmap: hot partition on shard-17.

eng-sre: logs show repeated routing decision churn where requests for model-redwood-2 get bounced between backends. suspected policy reweight loop after the rollout at 08:10.

iris: adding quick traces:
```
trace_id=ab12cd34 route=ingress-router-5 shard=17 backend=worker-5 latency=1450ms event=tail
trace_id=ab12cd35 route=ingress-router-5 shard=17 backend=worker-2 latency=1300ms event=tail
```

sam: that looks like misroute -> hot partition + head-of-line blocking. can we temporarily steer traffic away from shard-17?

mike: I'll create a live weight change to demote shard-17. doing: `rbctl set-weight shard-17 0.05 --region=euw2` (will post output)

ops-bot: command accepted. Applying weight change to routing table revision r314.

ops-bot: change applied: shard-17 weight=0.05 -> new routing distribution effective in ~15s.

ashley: after weight change p95 dropped ~120ms, p99 trending down but still ~850ms. streaming stalls reduced in number.

iris: looks better but tail still elevated. I see a fallback cascade: when shard-17 rejects, requests are being rerouted to shard-9/12 which are now getting overloaded. need a two-pronged approach: (1) stabilize policy rollout (rollback), (2) increase burst capacity on spare pool.

mike: roll back rollout at controller: `kubectl patch rollout/routing-policy -p '{"spec":{"version":"v1.1.2"}}'` rolling back to prior seed. Initiating canary rollback now.

eng-sre: telemetry: seed drift in router config generator caused weight oscillation every 30s. bug repro steps traced to policy-seed RNG change in last deploy. marking as root cause candidate.

sam: patch to temporary fix ready: pin routing-seed to stable hash and disable adaptive reweight for 10m: `api.post('/routing/config', {adaptive:false, seed:'stable-2026-03-15'})`

ops-bot: adaptive reweight disabled and seed pinned. New config applied.

ashley: re-evaluating queues: p99 now ~420ms, p95 ~120ms. streaming stalls significantly down; MediaCo reports sessions restored.

cs-lead: MediaCo confirms captioning backlog clearing, no new errors. leaving a follow-up support ticket to monitor for 24h. :white_check_mark:

iris: creating post-incident TODO: 1) revert weight hacks gradually, 2) full rollback of RNG seed change and run unit tests for policy stability, 3) add canary telemetry alert for reweight jitter, 4) run chaos test for hot partitions. I'll file the ticket.

eng-sre: I'll open a PR to add deterministic seed fallback and add a sim that asserts no >5% weight oscillation under load.

mike: oncall handoff in 30m — I'll stay until stable and then handoff to iris for overnight.

incident-bot: Incident severity: SEV2 -> degraded latency and partial product impact (streaming stalls). Status: mitigated (routing weight pin + rollback + bump capacity).

iris: quick timeline note for postmortem: 08:07 deploy with RNG change, 08:10 first p99 spike, 08:18 auto-escalation, 08:25 weight demotion applied, 08:33 adaptive pinned, 08:40 p99 back to <500ms.

sam: root cause hypothesis for postmortem: policy RNG change -> periodic seed rotation -> routing weight oscillation -> hot partitioning -> head-of-line tail latency -> cascade fallback overload.

mike: leaving final note: if anyone sees a recurrence ping me. tagging @eng-release to freeze rollout of routing-policy until fix merged.

ashley: added dashboards to show per-shard weight variance and per-route fallback count. will follow up with an alert runbook.

eng-sre: summary logs attached to ticket: `/var/log/router/2026-03-15/euw2.log` (sensitive) — will scrub and attach to postmortem.

cs-lead: scheduling customer follow-up for tomorrow morning with MediaCo.

incident-bot: Incident closed to active mitigation channel at 4012345800. Postmortem required.
